definition: In artificial intelligence and operations research, a regular constraint is a kind of global constraint.
details: It can be used to solve a particular type of puzzle called a nonogram or logigrams.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Regular constraint — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
